fields.Name: IT107 - Cache Architecture Invariants
fields.Description: Regression pins for the engine/cache/event-bus architecture work (plans/engine-cache-architecture-plan.md). CA1 asserts entities polled on a schedule with a time-varying filter are opted out of caching. CA2 runs the real User Routine dispatcher several times and asserts it writes no RunView cache slot, which is the pattern that filled 97% of one production Redis with write-only keys. CA3 checks the engine state census against the real AIEngineBase: its derived counts match the arrays, it reports derived state lost while every row array and identity hash is unchanged, and a reload reproduces every hash. CA4 saves several notes in one transaction and asserts the cached slot is untouched and reads miss until commit, holds every note after commit, and is invalidated (not written) when a transaction rolls back. CA5 interleaves failing and good statements, inside and outside a transaction, and asserts the provider stays usable. CA6 compares every loaded engine's cache key with the key its provider stores the rows under, with a row-filtered user as the control. CA7 submits several notes in one transaction group and asserts the cached slot is written once for the whole group, not once per row. CA8 submits a group mixing notes and action categories and asserts each entity's cached slot is written once and holds only its own rows. CA9 saves several action categories in a provider transaction and asserts the engine's cached slot is written once. CA10 submits a group that fails on a foreign key and asserts no cached slot is written and no rows remain; it guards the end-to-end outcome, since on SQL Server the failure happens before the batch opens. CA11 submits a group whose rows are linked by a transaction variable, then a group of deletes, and asserts each writes every cached slot once. CA2, CA4, CA5 and CA7–CA11 mutate — CA2 runs the real User Routine dispatcher (which claims and executes due routines), CA4 saves and rolls back notes, CA5 runs failing statements inside a transaction, CA7–CA11 save rows in a transaction group or a provider transaction — so all of them carry RequiresMutation and the bundle opts them in with runMutationTests; RUN_MUTATION_TESTS=1 gates them everywhere else. CA1, CA3 and CA6 read only.

ExpectedOutcomes.summary: Polled entities carry AllowCaching=false and repeated dispatcher sweeps leave the cache untouched. The census detects lost derived state that row counts and row hashes cannot. A transaction updates a cached slot once, on commit, and never with rolled-back rows. Failed statements do not strand connections. Every engine computes the cache key its provider stores the rows under.
